q: The metre gauge used on the older railway lines in India has a track width of:
e: The metre gauge used on older Indian railway lines has a track width of 1,000 mm, i.e., one metre between the rails, which gives the gauge its name.

q: The standard gauge, on which the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail corridor is being built, has a track width of:
e: The standard gauge has a track width of 1,435 mm; the Mumbai-Ahmedabad high-speed rail (bullet train) corridor is being built to this gauge, as used on Shinkansen lines.

q: The narrow gauge lines in India, such as the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, generally have a track width of:
e: Narrow gauge lines in India, such as the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, generally have a track width of 762 mm (2 feet 6 inches).

q: In an electric locomotive, the 'pantograph' is the device which:

options.A: Converts AC supply into DC supply
options.B: Connects the locomotive to the wagons behind it
options.D: Collects electric current from the overhead equipment wire and feeds it to the locomotive

e: The pantograph is the spring-loaded frame on the roof of an electric locomotive which presses against the overhead contact wire, collects electric current from it and feeds it to the locomotive.

q: In railway electrification, the abbreviation 'OHE' stands for:
e: In railway electrification, 'OHE' stands for Overhead Equipment, covering the contact and catenary wires, droppers, insulators and supporting structures above the track.

q: Which single commodity accounts for the largest share of the freight loading of Indian Railways?
e: Coal accounts for the largest share of the freight loading of Indian Railways, forming roughly half of its total originating freight traffic.

q: The Dhanbad division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Dhanbad division, a major coal-loading division, is a part of the East Central Railway, whose headquarters is at Hajipur.

q: The Sealdah division belongs to which zonal railway of Indian Railways?
e: The Sealdah division, serving Kolkata and its suburbs, belongs to the Eastern Railway headquartered at Kolkata.

q: The Madurai division is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Madurai division is administered by the Southern Railway, whose headquarters is at Chennai.

q: The train now known as the Golden Temple Mail was earlier famous by the name:
e: The train now known as the Golden Temple Mail was earlier famous as the Frontier Mail, which from 1928 ran between Bombay and Peshawar on the north-west frontier.

q: The historic Grand Trunk Express, introduced in 1929, runs between:
e: The historic Grand Trunk Express, introduced in 1929, runs between Chennai Central and New Delhi; it is one of the oldest long-distance trains of Indian Railways.

q: The Coromandel Express, running between Howrah and Chennai, derives its name from:

options.D: The Coromandel Coast of south-eastern India

e: The Coromandel Express, running between Howrah and Chennai, derives its name from the Coromandel Coast, the south-eastern coast of India along which much of its route lies.

q: The historic 'Boat Mail' (Indo-Ceylon Express) of the metre-gauge era was famous because it:

options.A: Connected Chennai with the ferry service to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) through Dhanushkodi
options.B: Carried boats on wagons to the ports
options.C: Ran entirely along the sea coast
options.D: Was hauled by a locomotive named 'Boat'

e: The historic 'Boat Mail' (Indo-Ceylon Express) was famous because it connected Chennai with the ferry service to Ceylon (Sri Lanka) through Dhanushkodi, forming a through rail-cum-sea link.

q: 'Sampark Kranti' Express trains were introduced with the main objective of:

options.A: Providing trains exclusively for military personnel
options.B: Providing faster connectivity between the State capitals and New Delhi
options.C: Connecting all district headquarters with the State capitals
options.D: Running tourist trains to religious places

e: 'Sampark Kranti' Express trains were introduced in 2004 with the main objective of providing faster connectivity between the State capitals and New Delhi with fewer stops.

q: 'Jan Shatabdi' Express trains, introduced as a variant of the Shatabdi class, are characterised by:

options.B: They run only on narrow gauge lines
options.C: They are affordable day trains having both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned chair car accommodation
options.D: They run exclusively during the night

e: 'Jan Shatabdi' Express trains are affordable day trains, a lower-fare variant of the Shatabdi class, having both air-conditioned and non-air-conditioned chair car accommodation.

q: The 'UDAY' Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.C: Trains run exclusively for school children
options.D: Overnight double-decker air-conditioned chair car trains on busy routes

e: 'UDAY' (Utkrisht Double-Decker Air-conditioned Yatri) Express trains are overnight double-decker air-conditioned chair car trains run on busy inter-city routes.

q: The 'Mahamana Express' of Indian Railways is named after:
e: The 'Mahamana Express' is named after Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya, the educationist and founder of Banaras Hindu University, who was popularly honoured with the title 'Mahamana'.

q: The 'August Kranti Rajdhani Express' gets its name from:

options.B: The 'August Kranti', i.e., the Quit India Movement launched in August 1942
options.C: The birth month of Mahatma Gandhi
options.D: The first session of the Indian National Congress

e: The 'August Kranti Rajdhani Express' gets its name from the 'August Kranti', i.e., the Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi in August 1942.

q: The Jaynagar-Kurtha cross-border railway link connects India with:
e: The Jaynagar-Kurtha cross-border railway link, the first broad-gauge cross-border link of its kind, connects India with Nepal.

q: The Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology (CAMTECH) of Indian Railways is located at:
e: The Centre for Advanced Maintenance Technology (CAMTECH), which develops improved maintenance practices and technologies for Indian Railways, is located at Gwalior in Madhya Pradesh.

q: One of the largest marshalling yards of Indian Railways is located at:
e: One of the largest marshalling yards of Indian Railways is located at Pt. Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Junction (formerly Mughalsarai) in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The Bhor Ghat, a steep gradient section where trains are assisted by banking locomotives, lies on the route between:
e: The Bhor Ghat is the steep gradient section between Karjat and Lonavala on the Mumbai-Pune route, where trains are assisted by banking (pusher) locomotives.

q: The Dudhsagar Falls, which can be seen from trains passing through the Braganza Ghat section, are located in the State of:
e: The Dudhsagar Falls, visible from trains passing through the Braganza Ghat section between Goa and Karnataka, are located in the State of Goa on the Mandovi river.

q: Oak Grove School at Jharipani, near Mussoorie, a well-known residential school, is run by:
e: Oak Grove School at Jharipani near Mussoorie is a well-known residential school run by Indian Railways (Northern Railway), originally for the children of railway employees.

q: The early railway lines in India in the 19th century were built mainly by:

options.A: Private British companies working under the Government's 'guarantee system'
options.B: The Public Works Department of the Government of India

e: The early railway lines in India in the 19th century were built mainly by private British companies working under the Government's 'guarantee system', which assured them a minimum return on capital.

q: The first section of the Delhi Metro, opened in December 2002, was between:
e: The Delhi Metro's first section, opened in December 2002, ran between Shahdara and Tis Hazari on what became the Red Line.

q: India's first luxury tourist train, the 'Palace on Wheels', was launched in the year:
e: India's first luxury tourist train, the 'Palace on Wheels', was launched in 1982 by Indian Railways in association with Rajasthan Tourism.

q: 'Super Vasuki', run by Indian Railways in August 2022, is famous as:

options.A: The fastest passenger train of India
options.B: The first train to run on hydrogen fuel
options.C: The first train operated entirely by women
options.D: The longest freight train ever run by Indian Railways

e: 'Super Vasuki', run by Indian Railways in August 2022, is famous as the longest freight train ever run by it, a 3.5 km long formation of 295 wagons hauled by five locomotives.

q: 'RailMadad' of Indian Railways is:

options.A: An integrated platform for lodging and tracking passenger grievances and enquiries
options.B: A scheme for free travel of senior citizens
options.C: A mobile application for booking unreserved tickets
options.D: A freight incentive scheme for bulk customers

e: 'RailMadad' is Indian Railways' integrated platform on which passengers can lodge and track grievances, enquiries and requests for assistance across all railway services.

q: The present system of five-digit train numbers on Indian Railways was introduced in the year:
e: The present system of five-digit train numbers, replacing the earlier four-digit numbers, was introduced by Indian Railways in December 2010.

q: The famous 'diamond crossing', where railway lines from four directions intersect at one place, is located at:
e: The famous 'diamond crossing', where railway lines from four directions intersect at one place, is located at Nagpur station in Maharashtra.

q: The full form of IRTS, an organised Group 'A' service of Indian Railways, is:
e: IRTS stands for Indian Railway Traffic Service, the organised Group 'A' service responsible for transportation (operations and commercial) functions on Indian Railways.

q: E. Sreedharan, who led the Konkan Railway and Delhi Metro projects, is popularly known as the:
e: E. Sreedharan, who led the Konkan Railway and Delhi Metro projects to timely completion, is popularly known as the 'Metro Man of India'.

q: In railway working, a 'break of gauge' occurs at a place where:

options.A: A train crosses from one railway zone to another
options.B: Two tracks of different gauges meet, requiring transhipment of passengers and goods
options.C: A level crossing is provided on the line
options.D: The track is damaged due to an accident

e: A 'break of gauge' occurs where two tracks of different gauges meet, so passengers and goods must be transhipped from one train to another to continue the journey.

q: India's first passenger train completed its historic run on the date:
e: India's first passenger train ran on 16 April 1853, covering 34 km from Bori Bunder (Mumbai) to Thane with 14 coaches and about 400 passengers.

q: In the context of Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'RMS' stands for:
e: In the context of Indian Railways, 'RMS' stands for Railway Mail Service, the wing which handles the carriage and sorting of mail on trains.

q: In railway operations, the abbreviation 'ART' stands for:
e: In railway operations, 'ART' stands for Accident Relief Train, a specially equipped train rushed to an accident site with cranes, tools and medical facilities.

q: 'Rail Nilayam' at Secunderabad is the headquarters building of:
e: 'Rail Nilayam' at Secunderabad is the headquarters building of the South Central Railway.

q: The southernmost railway station on the Indian Railways network is:
e: Kanyakumari is the southernmost railway station on the Indian Railways network, situated near the southern tip of the Indian peninsula.

q: Kathgodam, the terminal station of the broad-gauge line from the Bareilly side, is the principal railhead for the hill station of:
e: Kathgodam, the terminal broad-gauge railhead in the foothills of Kumaon, is the principal railway station serving the hill station of Nainital.

q: The railway station at Dhanushkodi in Tamil Nadu was destroyed and the line abandoned after:
e: The railway station at Dhanushkodi in Tamil Nadu was destroyed, and the line abandoned, after the devastating cyclonic storm of December 1964.

q: The first Duronto Express, introduced in 2009, ran between:
e: The first Duronto Express, introduced in 2009 as a non-stop point-to-point service, ran between Sealdah and New Delhi.

q: The historic Kalka Mail, among India's oldest trains, was renamed in 2021 as:
e: The historic Kalka Mail, among India's oldest running trains, was renamed in January 2021 as the Netaji Express in honour of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

q: The 'Charminar Express', running between Hyderabad and Chennai, is named after:

options.D: The Charminar, the iconic monument of Hyderabad

e: The 'Charminar Express', running between Hyderabad and Chennai, is named after the Charminar, the iconic 16th-century monument of Hyderabad.

q: The Brindavan Express, one of the earliest intercity trains of South India, runs between:
e: The Brindavan Express, one of the earliest intercity trains of South India, introduced in 1964, runs between Chennai Central and KSR Bengaluru.

q: The Preamble to the Constitution of India begins with the words:

options.C: We, the Representatives of the People
options.D: We, the Members of the Constituent Assembly

e: The Preamble to the Constitution of India begins with the words 'We, the People of India', indicating that the Constitution derives its authority from the people.

q: Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as a:
e: Article 1 of the Constitution describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States', emphasising that the Union is indestructible though the States are not.

q: Article 21 of the Constitution of India guarantees the:

options.C: Right to Life and Personal Liberty

e: Article 21 of the Constitution guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty, providing that no person shall be deprived of these except according to procedure established by law.

q: The power of the President of India to grant pardons, reprieves and remissions of punishment is conferred by:
e: The power of the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment is conferred by Article 72 of the Constitution.

q: The Governor of a State in India is appointed by the:
e: The Governor of a State is appointed by the President of India under Article 155 and holds office during the pleasure of the President.

q: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha is:
e: The minimum age prescribed for a person to be chosen as a member of the Lok Sabha is 25 years, as laid down in Article 84 of the Constitution.

q: The concept of the Concurrent List in the Indian Constitution has been borrowed from the Constitution of:
e: The concept of the Concurrent List, on which both Parliament and State Legislatures may legislate, has been borrowed in the Indian Constitution from the Constitution of Australia.

q: Panchayati Raj was first implemented in India in 1959 in the State of:
e: Panchayati Raj was first implemented in India on 2 October 1959 in the Nagaur district of Rajasthan, inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.

q: A Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 has so far been issued in India:
e: A Proclamation of National Emergency under Article 352 has so far been issued in India three times - in 1962, 1971 and 1975.

q: In the proceedings of Parliament, the 'Zero Hour' refers to the period that:

options.C: Is allotted for voting on Demands for Grants
options.D: Is reserved for the discussion of the Budget

e: In Parliament, the 'Zero Hour' is the period immediately following the Question Hour, during which members raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice.

q: The Mansabdari system of administration was introduced by the Mughal emperor:
e: The Mansabdari system, a ranking system grading nobles and military officers under the Mughals, was introduced by the emperor Akbar.

q: Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore, was killed in 1799 while defending:
e: Tipu Sultan, the ruler of Mysore, was killed in 1799 while defending Seringapatam during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

q: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Lucknow was led by:
e: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Lucknow was led by Begum Hazrat Mahal, who proclaimed her son Birjis Qadr as the ruler of Awadh.

q: The first session of the Indian National Congress, held in December 1885, was convened at:
e: The first session of the Indian National Congress, held in December 1885 with W. C. Bonnerjee as president, was convened at Bombay.

q: The Rowlatt Act, against which Mahatma Gandhi launched an all-India satyagraha, was passed in the year:
e: The Rowlatt Act, which allowed detention of political prisoners without trial, was passed in 1919; Mahatma Gandhi launched an all-India satyagraha against it.

q: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of 1931, the Indian National Congress agreed to suspend the:
e: Under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931, the Indian National Congress agreed to suspend the Civil Disobedience Movement and to participate in the Second Round Table Conference.

q: The popular slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' was given by:
e: The popular slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan', honouring the soldier and the farmer, was given by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1965.

q: The first Indian to succeed in joining the Indian Civil Service (ICS) was:
e: Satyendranath Tagore, brother of Rabindranath Tagore, was the first Indian to succeed in joining the Indian Civil Service, in 1863.

q: The ancient seat of learning, Takshashila (Taxila), is located in the present-day country of:
e: The ancient seat of learning Takshashila (Taxila), famous for its university of Vedic and later Buddhist learning, is located in present-day Pakistan.

q: The famous 'Great Bath' of the Indus Valley Civilisation has been excavated at:
e: The famous 'Great Bath', a large ritual bathing tank of the Indus Valley Civilisation, has been excavated at Mohenjo-daro in present-day Pakistan.

q: The river Brahmaputra originates from:
e: The Brahmaputra originates from glaciers in Tibet, near Lake Mansarovar, and flows eastward as the Yarlung Tsangpo before entering India through Arunachal Pradesh.

q: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at the:
e: The Western Ghats and the Eastern Ghats meet at the Nilgiri Hills in Tamil Nadu, where the hill station of Ooty (Udhagamandalam) is located.

q: The Dal Lake, a famous tourist attraction, is situated in the city of:
e: The Dal Lake, a famous tourist attraction known for its houseboats and shikaras, is situated in the city of Srinagar in Jammu and Kashmir.

q: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built across the river:
e: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, one of the largest masonry dams in the world, is built across the river Krishna on the Telangana-Andhra Pradesh border.

q: Which State of India has the largest forest cover in terms of area?
e: Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest cover in terms of area among the States of India, according to the India State of Forest Reports.

q: The city of Ahmedabad is popularly known as the:
e: Ahmedabad is popularly known as the 'Manchester of India' because of its once-dominant cotton textile industry, comparable to Manchester of England.

q: The Great Indian Desert of north-western India is known as the:
e: The Great Indian Desert of north-western India, spread mainly over western Rajasthan, is known as the Thar Desert.

q: The highest waterfall in India is the:
e: The highest waterfall in India is the Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka, formed by the Varahi river, with a total height of about 455 metres.

q: The First Five-Year Plan of India accorded the highest priority to:
e: The First Five-Year Plan (1951-56) accorded the highest priority to agriculture and irrigation, along with power, to overcome food shortage and revive the economy.

q: Disguised unemployment, where more persons are engaged in a work than are actually needed, is most commonly found in the:
e: Disguised unemployment, where more persons are engaged in a work than are actually needed so that removing some would not reduce output, is most commonly found in the agricultural sector.

q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on the recommendations of the:
e: The Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance).

q: The largest public sector bank of India is the:
e: The State Bank of India is the largest public sector bank of India, with the biggest network of branches, deposits and advances among Indian banks.

q: 'Devaluation' of a currency means:

options.A: An official reduction in the external value of the currency by the Government
options.B: A fall in the purchasing power of money due to inflation
options.C: Replacement of old currency notes with new ones
options.D: A reduction in the bank rate by the central bank

e: 'Devaluation' of a currency means an official reduction in the external value of the currency by the Government or central bank, making exports cheaper and imports costlier.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Goods and Services Tax (GST) is a destination-based indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services.
2. GST was introduced in India through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: GST is a destination-based indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services, and it was introduced in India through the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016, with effect from 1 July 2017.

q: The pH value of pure water at ordinary temperature is:
e: The pH value of pure water at ordinary temperature is 7, which is neutral on the pH scale - neither acidic nor alkaline.

q: The chemical symbol of gold is:
e: The chemical symbol of gold is 'Au', derived from 'aurum', the Latin name for gold.

q: The planet nearest to the Sun is:
e: Mercury is the planet nearest to the Sun, completing one revolution around it in about 88 days.

q: The branch of science that deals with the study of fungi is called:
e: Mycology is the branch of science (biology) that deals with the study of fungi, including mushrooms, moulds and yeasts.

q: The vitamin which the human body can synthesise in the skin with the help of sunlight is:
e: Vitamin D is the vitamin which the human body can synthesise in the skin with the help of sunlight; it is therefore also called the 'sunshine vitamin'.

q: The BCG vaccine is administered to protect against:
e: The BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guerin) vaccine is administered, usually at birth, to protect against tuberculosis.

q: 'Heavy water', used as a moderator in nuclear reactors, is chemically:

options.A: Water with a high mineral content

e: 'Heavy water', used as a moderator in nuclear reactors to slow down neutrons, is chemically deuterium oxide (D2O), in which hydrogen is replaced by its heavier isotope deuterium.

q: The famous Bengali novel 'Pather Panchali' was written by:
e: The famous Bengali novel 'Pather Panchali', depicting rural Bengali life through the child Apu, was written by Bibhutibhushan Bandopadhyay; Satyajit Ray later filmed it.

q: The legendary Indian athlete Milkha Singh was popularly known as the:
e: The legendary Indian athlete Milkha Singh, the champion sprinter who finished fourth in the 400 m at the 1960 Rome Olympics, was popularly known as the 'Flying Sikh'.

q: Teachers' Day, celebrated in India on 5th September, marks the birth anniversary of:

options.A: Dr. A. P. J. Abdul Kalam

e: Teachers' Day, celebrated in India on 5th September, marks the birth anniversary of Dr. S. Radhakrishnan, the philosopher-statesman who became the second President of India.

q: The first woman to be honoured with the Bharat Ratna was:
e: Indira Gandhi, honoured in 1971, was the first woman to receive the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian award.

q: The world's first public railway worked by steam locomotives, opened in 1825, ran between:
e: The world's first public railway worked by steam locomotives, opened in 1825, ran between Stockton and Darlington in England; it was engineered by George Stephenson.

q: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Railways' for his pioneering work on steam locomotives and the first public railway?
e: George Stephenson is regarded as the 'Father of Railways' for his pioneering work on steam locomotives, including the 'Rocket', and for building the first public steam railway.

q: The world's first underground (metro) railway, opened in 1863, was built in the city of:
e: The world's first underground (metro) railway, the Metropolitan Railway opened in 1863, was built in the city of London.

q: The longest railway line in the world, connecting Moscow with Vladivostok, is the:
e: The longest railway line in the world is the Trans-Siberian Railway, connecting Moscow with Vladivostok over a distance of about 9,289 km.

q: The world's first high-speed 'bullet train' service, the Shinkansen, was introduced in 1964 in:
e: The world's first high-speed 'bullet train' service, the Shinkansen, was introduced in 1964 in Japan, timed with the Tokyo Olympics.

q: In railway security, the 'GRP', which functions as a wing of the State Police, stands for:
e: In railway security, 'GRP' stands for Government Railway Police, the wing of the State Police responsible for law and order and investigation of crimes on railway premises and trains.

q: The battalion-level striking force of the Railway Protection Force, raised for special security duties, is known as the:
e: The battalion-level striking force of the Railway Protection Force, raised for special security duties such as election and anti-sabotage work, is known as the Railway Protection Special Force (RPSF).

q: The headquarters of the Commission of Railway Safety is located at:
e: The headquarters of the Commission of Railway Safety, which inquires into serious train accidents, is located at Lucknow; it functions under the Ministry of Civil Aviation.

q: The principal bench (headquarters) of the Railway Claims Tribunal is located at:
e: The principal bench (headquarters) of the Railway Claims Tribunal, which decides compensation claims for train accidents and untoward incidents, is located at Delhi.

q: The Railways Act, 1989 replaced the earlier Indian Railways Act which was enacted in the year:
e: The Railways Act, 1989, which came into force on 1 July 1990, replaced the earlier Indian Railways Act enacted in the year 1890.
